structures.overall_structure: κ-carbide (j-carbide) hardened austenitic low-density steel; austenitic matrix with κ-carbides formed during quenching

unmapped_findings: The κ-carbide (j-carbide) phase of the Fe-26Mn-11Al-1.2C alloy can act as hydrogen trap sites with an estimated activation energy of ~76–80 kJ/mol (from a Redlich–Kister analysis of thermal desorption at 26 K/min). Note: this trapping energy was measured on hydrogen-charged specimens of the same alloy (thermal desorption analysis), so it characterizes the alloy's κ-carbide phase rather than the uncharged condition itself.

For this κ-carbide hardened austenitic low-density steel, hydrogen-assisted damage was reported to occur by cracking at grain boundary triple junctions and by chains of microvoids forming on grain boundaries under pronounced planar slip localization (linked to κ-carbides). These mechanisms pertain to the hydrogen-charged condition, not to the uncharged reference specimen.
